svg.title: Inside an LLM: layers, heads and the KV cache
svg.desc: An LLM is a stack of identical transformer layers: layer 1, layer 2, and so on up to layer N (12 in GPT-2). The tokens "The cat sat on the" enter at the bottom. Inside every layer, multi-head attention runs many heads side by side (head 1 to head 12 in GPT-2), and each head makes its own Q, K and V. Then a feed-forward network works on each token alone. Next to every layer sits its own KV cache: a K row and a V row for every earlier token. Each new token saves its K and V into the cache and reuses the stored ones, so past tokens are never recomputed. Q is only needed for the newest token, so it isn't cached. At the top, linear and softmax pick the next token, "mat". Values are illustrative.
svg.text: Inside an LLM: layers, heads and the KV cache
A stack of identical layers. Every layer runs many attention heads, each making Q, K and V, and keeps its own cache of past K and V.
what the new token is looking for (not cached)
what each token offers to be found by
Each new token computes Q, K, V once per head per layer, saves its K and V, and reuses everyone else’s from the cache. Values are illustrative.
